newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia opens direct phone link with N.America.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia opens direct phone link with N.America.

text.p: Cambodia on Friday started direct telecommunications links to Canada and the United States with the commissioning of a new earth station.
The F3 Satellite Earth Station was installed by Australia's Telstra Corp under a business cooperation contract with Cambodia's Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications (MPTC).

The earth station was formally opened by MPTC Secretary of State So Khun and Telstra's general manager for Indochina, Mara Moustafine, who said the new technology would help meet growth in traffic demand and save on transit and space segment charges.

The new earth station provides Cambodia with access to Pacific Ocean satellites. It supplies direct links to the United States and Canada, while links to other Pacific nations can be opened when required.
The earth station complements the Bayon Standard A satellite earth station, which has access to Indian Ocean satellites, a Telstra statement said.
The commissioning of the satellite link follows a decision to cut overseas the prices of telephone calls from February 1, So Khun said.

The rate to Laos and Thailand will drop 20 cents to $3.20 per minute, the current rate for calls to Vietnam, while the tariff for other Asian countries is to drop to $3.40 per minute from $3.80. Calls to all other countries will cost $3.80 per minute against the current $4.20.

"I hope the improvement in the telecommunications quality to the USA and Canada from today and the reduced tariff rates from February 1 will enhance all relationships, including business, between our two countries," So Khun said.
